title: Opposites Make Zero
short: A number and its opposite add to 0.

blocks.html: In Grade 6 you met opposites: $3$ and $-3$ are the same distance from $0$, on opposite sides. This lesson is about what happens when you add them. It is the key to adding any signed numbers.
A number plus its opposite is zero: $a + (-a) = 0$. A $+1$ and a $-1$ together make a zero pair.

Adding a positive number moves you right on the number line; adding a negative number moves you left. Start at $0$, move 5 right, then 5 left: you are back at $0$. With money it is the same: earn \$5, spend \$5, and you have the same amount as before.

blocks.name: integerline
blocks.cap: $5 + (-5)$: five steps right, then five steps left, back to $0$.

blocks.name: counters
blocks.cap: Yellow counters are $+1$ and red counters are $-1$. Use 8 counters in all to show $-2$.

blocks.title: Spotting a zero pair
steps: $6$ and $-6$ are opposites, so together they make $0$.

blocks.title: Counters
blocks.q: A bag holds 7 positive counters and 4 negative counters. What number does it show?
steps: Match each negative counter with a positive one: 4 zero pairs, worth $0$.
3 positive counters are left over, so the bag shows $3$.

blocks.html: This is why the number of counters can change while the value stays the same: adding a zero pair (one $+1$ and one $-1$) adds nothing.
